17D.7 You are not to trust in the abundance of your riches, for he who trusts in his riches will fall.

precepts.text: The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock; this is a proud man.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
“Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man?” This psalm was written when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul that David had come to the house of Ahimelech. Obadiah speaks to Edom: “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” This is a proud man, the boasting mighty man of Psalm 52.

The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that. The pride of Esau's heart has deceived him, and he thinks no one will bring him down.

precepts.text: He said in his heart he would ascend into heaven, exalt his throne above the stars of God, and sit upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
“For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”. This is the boasting of the mighty man. He said in his heart he would ascend into heaven, exalt his throne above the stars of God, and sit upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north.

The congregation is the congregation of the Lord, Israel, and the north is where he rules over them. Esau boasts that he will sit over the Most High's congregation. That is the pride of heart that deceived him, and the man of sin has to be revealed for who he is.

precepts.text: The congregation of the Lord in the sight of all Israel; Esau boasts he will rule over the congregation of the Most High in the north, and Israel is the audience of the Bible.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
David spoke “in the sight of all Israel the congregation of the Lord, and in the audience of our God”, charging them to “keep and seek for all the commandments of the Lord your God: that ye may possess this good land, and leave it for an inheritance for your children after you for ever.” All Israel is the congregation of the Lord, and Israel is the audience of the Bible.

So when Lucifer says he will sit upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north, that is Esau boasting he will rule over the congregation of the Most High, Israel, in the north. He boasts himself in mischief over the very people the Most High gave the commandments and the good land to.

precepts.text: He said, I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.” That is the boast of the mighty man in his mischief: he will be like the most High. This is why Esau paints Christ white and makes himself the image of God; he said in his heart he would be like the most High. Our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, but here is his own boast, and the pride of his heart has deceived him.

precepts.text: "Ho, ho" is what he says coming through; flee from the land of the north where he rules over the Israelites, scattered abroad as the four winds.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.” Ho, ho is what he says coming through. Lucifer boasted he would sit on the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north, and here the Most High tells Israel to flee from the land of the north, where Esau rules over the Israelites who were spread abroad as the four winds of the heaven.

The boasting mighty man rules over the scattered congregation in the north for now, but the Most High is calling his people out of that land.

precepts.text: Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon; this America is mystery Babylon.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Zion, Israel, is dwelling with the daughter of Babylon, and this America is mystery Babylon. The land of the north where the mighty man boasts over the congregation is the daughter of Babylon, and the Most High says deliver thyself out of her. That is the call to Israel scattered under Esau's rule.

precepts.text: Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.” The one who said in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground, who boasted he would ascend into heaven and be like the most High, is brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit. The mighty man boasting himself in mischief ends there. The pride of his heart deceived him, and the Most High brings him down.

precepts.text: They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble; Satan is a man, Lucifer is a man.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
“They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”. Is this the man. Satan is a man; Lucifer is a man. The mighty man of Psalm 52 who boasts himself in mischief is looked upon narrowly when he is brought down, and the ones who see him ask, is this the man that made the earth to tremble and shook kingdoms?

That is the man of sin revealed. Our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ, but the scriptures call him a man.

precepts.text: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer; the man of sin is revealed as a man, not a horned figure with a pitchfork.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” Lucifer, who said he would ascend into heaven and be like the most High, is fallen and cut down to the ground. He weakened the nations.

The man of sin is revealed as a man, not a horned figure with a pitchfork. The white picture of Jesus is a deception, and the devil is Esau, the boasting mighty man who dwells in the clefts of the rock and rules over the congregation in the north. The Bible says nothing of a horned devil; it says, is this the man.

precepts.text: He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him; he hath broken his covenant.
precepts.point: Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs, like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs; like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.” Psalm 55 shows the same man: “He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him: he hath broken his covenant.” He puts forth his hands against those at peace with him and breaks his covenant. That is the deceitful working of the razor tongue: peace in the mouth, and a broken covenant behind it.

precepts.text: The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart; the white man promises reparations and forty acres and a mule, but breaks his covenant.
precepts.point: Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs, like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.” That is the tongue like a sharp razor, working deceitfully. The white man promises reparations and forty acres and a mule, words smoother than butter and softer than oil, but war is in his heart and he breaks his covenant. His soft words are drawn swords.

precepts.text: They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble; the righteous will marvel that he is brought to nothing.
precepts.point: The righteous also shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “The righteous also shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him”. Isaiah shows what they see: “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”. The righteous will look narrowly on the boasting mighty man when he is brought down and marvel that he is brought to nothing. Is this the man that made the earth to tremble? That is why they laugh at him.

precepts.text: The kings of the earth who committed fornication with Babylon bewail her.
precepts.point: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness. He trusted in his slave trades and his riches.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength; but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness.” He trusted in his slave trades and his riches. Revelation shows where that trust ends: “the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning”. The kings who fornicated with Babylon and lived deliciously with her will bewail her when the riches burn.

precepts.text: Standing afar off for fear of her torment, saying, Alas, that great city Babylon, for in one hour is thy judgment come.
precepts.point: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness. He trusted in his slave trades and his riches.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: They stand “afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.” The man who trusted in the abundance of his riches and strengthened himself in his wickedness sees his mighty city judged in one hour. All the riches from the slave trades could not make God his strength, and the kings stand afar off in fear.

precepts.text: The merchants of the earth weep and mourn, for no man buyeth their merchandise any more.
precepts.point: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness. He trusted in his slave trades and his riches.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more”. The riches he trusted in were built on merchandise, and when no man buys it any more, the merchants weep and mourn. This is the man that made not God his strength: when the trade stops, his strength is gone.

precepts.text: The merchandise of gold, silver, precious stones, pearls, fine linen, purple, silk, and scarlet; we no longer buy purple, which represents royalty, from the white man.
precepts.point: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness. He trusted in his slave trades and his riches.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: The merchandise is listed: “gold, and silver, and precious stones, and of pearls, and fine linen, and purple, and silk, and scarlet, and all thyine wood, and all manner vessels of ivory”, and vessels of most precious wood, brass, iron and marble. Purple represents royalty, and we no longer buy purple from the white man. The abundance of riches the mighty man trusted in is this merchandise, and the merchants mourn because no man buys it any more.

precepts.text: Cinnamon, odours, ointments, frankincense, wine, oil, fine flour, wheat, beasts, sheep, horses, chariots, and slaves, and souls of men; Israel was the first commodity on Wall Street.
precepts.point: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness. He trusted in his slave trades and his riches.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “And cinnamon, and odours, and ointments, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat, and beasts, and sheep, and horses, and chariots, and slaves, and souls of men.” At the end of Babylon's merchandise are slaves and souls of men. Israel was the first commodity on Wall Street. That is the slave trade the man of Psalm 52 trusted in, the abundance of riches he strengthened himself in his wickedness with, and it is what the merchants weep over when the judgment comes in one hour.

precepts.text: The Lord called thy name a green olive tree, fair and of goodly fruit; we are that green olive tree.
precepts.point: But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God; I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God: I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.” Jeremiah tells who the green olive tree is: “The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit”. We are that green olive tree. The Lord called Israel by that name, fair and of goodly fruit, and though “with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken”, David stands as the green olive tree in the house of God, trusting in his mercy for ever.

precepts.text: How shall we be able to magnify him, for he is great above all his works?
precepts.point: I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it; and I will wait on thy name, for it is good before thy saints.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it”. “How shall we be able to magnify him? for he is great above all his works.” He is great above all his works, so how can we magnify him enough? David's answer is to praise him for ever and wait on his name, for it is good before his saints.

precepts.text: When you glorify the Most High, exalt him as much as you can, for he far exceeds; put forth all your strength and be not weary, for you can never go far enough.
precepts.point: I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it; and I will wait on thy name, for it is good before thy saints.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
“When ye glorify the Lord, exalt him as much as ye can; for even yet will he far exceed: and when ye exalt him, put forth all your strength, and be not weary; for ye can never go far enough.” Exalt the Most High as much as you can, for he far exceeds it; put forth all your strength and be not weary, for you can never go far enough.

That is why David says “I will praise thee for ever”. Praise for ever is the only fitting measure for one great above all his works, and waiting on his name is good before his saints.
